b23c1694-7f92-438e-bca4-10de9dbd63b3.case_title: Vishnoo Mittal vs M/S. Shakti Trading Company
orders: The Supreme Court granted leave to appeal and observed that the High Court erred in its reliance on the P. Mohan Raj precedent because the cause of action in the present case arose after the imposition of a moratorium under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
preview_summary: The Supreme Court distinguished the present case from P. Mohan Raj, noting that the cause of action for the Negotiable Instruments Act (NI Act) offence arose only after the insolvency commencement date and the imposition of a moratorium under Section 14 of the IBC.

The Court clarified that under Section 138 of the NI Act, the cause of action is only completed when the drawer fails to make payment within fifteen days of receipt of a demand notice, which in this instance occurred while the moratorium was already in effect.

The dispute originates from a 1918 application under the Poorer Classes Accommodation Scheme (PCAS) involving land intended for worker dwellings, which has been the subject of multiple statutory transitions and a 51-year period of inaction regarding conveyance.

preview_summary: The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's acquittal of the respondents in a kidnapping and murder case, affirming that the prosecution failed to establish a complete chain of circumstantial evidence.

The Court clarified that the 'last seen together' theory under Section 106 of the Evidence Act is insufficient for conviction unless the prosecution proves all other incriminating circumstances beyond reasonable doubt.
